unit_title: Route the packaged-regression blocker to its closed owners

dispatch_history.contribution: Produced the owner chain, the single authorised unmodified packaged gate run, the discarded runtime sidecar, the RC-1..RC-7 structural root-cause chain, and the first machine route of the four owning requirement IDs.

Proved, by executing the controller's own parser and the controller's own documented findings derivation, that a v2 fragment result structurally cannot carry a findings array, and that route_findings is not invoked at the unit_run node at all. Repositioned the routable payload inside the controller's authoritative[-1600:] findings window and corrected the pivot order to W16 -> W20 -> W55. Did not re-run the spent gate run.

controller_routing_reachability.summary: The closed-owner repair transaction that this unit is scoped to produce cannot be opened from the unit_run node by any worker output. This is a property of the maintained controller, proven from its own source and reproduced with its own parser, not an inference from prose.
falsified_hypotheses_this_supersedes: Writing a wave-local routing artifact routes the Wave. It does not: the controller reads no worker-written artifact when deciding routing.

A worker can hand the controller a findings list. It cannot: the v2 fragment contract admits only status, meta and handoff fragments, and set(data) is strictly validated, so result['findings'] is structurally absent for every opencode text-backend phase.

controller_source_findings.finding: _parse_fragment_machine_result builds result from status/meta/handoff only and never assigns a findings key. Verified by execution: the maintained parser, imported and run against this dispatch's exact result text, returned HAS_FINDINGS_KEY=False.

The controller's own findings source is therefore the fallback [str(x) for x in (machine.get('findings') or []) ...] or [authoritative[-1600:]], i.e. the last 1600 characters of the worker's authoritative stdout. This is why the 0006 receipt's findings field is a mangled prose tail rather than a list.

route_findings is invoked only for wave_audit/close with status != PASS, and for repair with status not in {READY_FOR_AUDIT, PASS, READY}. The unit_run node is not a routing trigger, and closed_owner_repair_transaction events are emitted only inside the routed branch at :6049-6055.

routed_owner sorts candidate closed owners ascending by wave number, so the controller pivot is the lowest-numbered closed owner, W16, not W55. The 0006 resume_point and the inherited unit_plan premise both named W55 first; that ordering is wrong.

choose_after('run', 'REOPEN') returns 'repair'. The repair node is one of the two routing-capable nodes, so REOPEN from unit_run is the only worker-controllable lever that moves the node machine toward a node where the transaction can actually be opened.

executed_evidence.oracle: .opencode/scripts/run-wave-program.py imported as a module and used as its own parser; no reimplementation of the derivation.

premise_correction.plan_handoff_claimed: maintained unmodified gate returns FAIL 1/20 while the runtime sidecar it discards reports result=PASS phase=4
premise_correction.measured_at_this_dispatch: maintained unmodified gate returned PASS 20/20 while the runtime sidecar it discards reports result=PASS phase=4 together with its own clean_shutdown=FAIL and pty_resize=FAIL
premise_correction.consequence: The gate/sidecar relationship is the inverse of the plan premise. The gate green is not evidence of the artifact's own shutdown or resize behaviour, so HPC-W10-PKGREG-001 cannot be closed on this run. The recorded red is the artifact's own self-report, not the gate verdict.

root_cause_chain.statement: The packaged runtime probe seeds checks['pty_resize'] = 'FAIL' as a literal default.
root_cause_chain.proof: Select-String over src/hpc_gui/wx_shell.py for pty_resize and clean_shutdown returns exactly the literal seeds at 1994 and 1997 plus the unrelated fresh-user probe at 1563/1568/1594/1595; no assignment sets either key to PASS inside _run_packaged_smoke.

root_cause_chain.statement: The packaged runtime probe seeds checks['clean_shutdown'] = 'FAIL' as a literal default and never closes it, so the artifact's own clean_shutdown self-report is a constant FAIL.
root_cause_chain.proof: Same Select-String sweep; the only checks['clean_shutdown'] = 'PASS' in the file is at line 1595, inside the separate fresh-user probe whose own state dict is initialised at 1588.

root_cause_chain.statement: The packaged probe hardcodes state['result'] = 'PASS' at the single point where the phase-4 terminal readback and the transfer-queue render succeed. It is not derived from the checks dict. The sibling fresh-user probe does derive it, at line 1625, so the two probes in the same file disagree on the meaning of result.
root_cause_chain.proof: Every state["result"] assignment inside _run_packaged_smoke is the initial FAIL at 2002, the payload field read at 2030, the write-failure FAIL at 2052, and the hardcoded PASS at 2479.

root_cause_chain.statement: main() returns the packaged process exit code from smoke_state['result'], which is the hardcoded field of RC-3. The child exit code therefore carries no shutdown information beyond the phase-4 readback.
root_cause_chain.proof: return 0 if smoke_state["result"] == "PASS" else 1, reading the same state object written at 2479.

root_cause_chain.statement: The gate hard-excludes process_started, clean_shutdown and pty_resize from the copy of the artifact's own runtime checks, so the two constant FAILs of RC-1 and RC-2 can never reach the gate report.
root_cause_chain.proof: for name in REQUIRED_CHECKS: if name in ("process_started", "clean_shutdown", "pty_resize"): continue

root_cause_chain.statement: The gate re-derives pty_resize only from the disposable loopback SSH server's observed wire sizes, so the gate's pty_resize is a harness observation and never the artifact's own resize report.
root_cause_chain.proof: if any(size[0:2] == (96, 31) for size in loopback_server.pty_sizes) and any(size[0:2] == (123, 45) for size in loopback_server.resize_sizes): checks['pty_resize'] = 'PASS'

root_cause_chain.statement: The gate derives clean_shutdown from returncode == 0 and isolated and runtime.get('result') == 'PASS'. By RC-4 the returncode is itself a function of runtime['result'], so the check is partly tautological and its remaining discriminating power is only returncode and src-isolation. The artifact's own clean_shutdown=FAIL is never consulted.
root_cause_chain.proof: checks["clean_shutdown"] = "PASS" if returncode == 0 and isolated and runtime.get("result") == "PASS" else "FAIL"

acceptance_condition_for_owner_repair.statement: A packaged clean_shutdown proof requires the artifact's own runtime probe to set checks['clean_shutdown'] to PASS on evidence of completed teardown, and the gate must fail the run when the artifact's own check is FAIL. Equivalently: the gate result must not be reachable while the sidecar the same gate reads still reports clean_shutdown=FAIL.

non_remedies: Do not edit src/hpc_gui/wx_shell.py to make the probe set clean_shutdown or pty_resize to PASS; that manufactures acceptance evidence in a Wave that owns no product code.
Do not edit scripts/wx_packaged_smoke.py to widen the REQUIRED_CHECKS copy loop or to add the excluded keys; that would launder a constant FAIL into a gate PASS.
Do not raise the gate timeout to chase the previously observed post-PASS non-termination; the single run at this content identity completed in 10.5s with returncode 0, far below any timeout.
Do not relax, skip or xfail any test to obtain a green.
Do not author the W57 evidence manifest or a green FREEZE-046 freeze declaration while HPC-W10-PKGREG-001 is open.
Do not rebuild or patch dist/hpc-client-gui/hpc-client-gui.exe; the owner correction must be followed by an owner-driven rebuild and a fresh identity.
Do not re-test the falsified budget, stale-candidate, foreground or desktop-contaminant hypotheses; this unit contributes a source-proven structural cause instead.
